agents.emperor: Decided the structure: 6 queens (one per subdomain: ground truth, sequencing, algorithms, databases, evaluation, decisions), 1 king (cross-domain analogies and serendipity), 1 completeness critic. Queens do not talk to each other; only the king links them, to keep each context small.
agents.king: Forces cross-domain analogies (law, medicine, art, philosophy) and 'how others overcame it' stories.
agents.critic: Re-opens cited sources and flags anything stated as fact that is not supported.

entries.title: Plan written into the repo
entries.story: Before any code, PLAN.md fixed the question (which classifier should I trust, and what should I check?), the data, the tools, the metrics and the report format.

entries.title: Ground truth read from the vendor datasheet, not memory
entries.story: The source paper says 'eight bacteria at 12%' but not on what basis. The research agents claimed the 12% was DNA, not cells, and the critic could not confirm their cell-share numbers. So the vendor's datasheet table was extracted directly from two independent copies: 12% and 2% are theoretical genomic DNA, and by cell number the same tube is very different (L. fermentum 21.9%, the yeasts 0.29% and 0.18%; the cell column sums to 99.9%). Tools that report reads are now scored against DNA, and tools that report cells against cells.

entries.title: No local Linux tooling
entries.story: This Windows machine has no WSL distribution and Docker's engine returned an error, so the classifiers cannot run locally. Decision: run them on the Explorer cluster (public 'short' partition only) and keep only small result tables in git.

entries.title: SSH refused the config file
entries.story: ssh rejected the user config because Windows gave 'Everyone' full access to it. Instead of changing the user's permissions, a private copy of the config (no secrets) was used for this session.

entries.title: Reads streamed, never downloaded in full
entries.story: Only the first N read pairs of each run were streamed from ENA (12 samples, under 1 GB in total). No FASTQ is committed.

entries.title: Setup bugs, found by running it
entries.story: 1) Slurm runs a copy of the script so relative paths broke. 2) MetaPhlAn needs Python 3.11 because Python 3.12+ removed a module it imports. 3) A check tested for a folder, not its contents, so an empty database folder looked finished. 4) MetaPhlAn 4.x renamed two flags. Each was fixed and committed.

entries.title: A silent empty file nearly corrupted one result
entries.story: For the log mock, the second mate of the read pair downloaded as an empty file, yet the fetch script reported success because it only counted the first mate. Kraken2 then wrote empty reports without failing. It was caught because Bracken crashed on the empty report. The fetch script now verifies both mates match and retries.

entries.title: All 12 samples classified
entries.story: Kraken2 (2 databases x 2 confidence settings), Bracken and MetaPhlAn 4 ran on every sample on the public queue.

entries.title: Surprising results were checked before being believed
entries.story: Only 3% to 38% of Kraken2 reads looked species-level, which seemed too low. Checking the raw report showed 97% were classified, but many stopped at genus level (218,000 reads at Listeria genus, 13,000 at the species) because close relatives make the evidence ambiguous. A real property of the method, not a bug.

entries.title: A naming trap found and reported both ways
entries.story: All six methods labelled the single Bacillus subtilis isolate as Bacillus spizizenii, a former subspecies now treated as a species. Strict scoring counts that as a miss, so the headline stays strict and a clearly labelled relaxed score is shown beside it.

entries.title: Decision report written
entries.story: REPORT.md gives a recommendation by use case, then for every run what the result supports, what it does not, and what to check next. Claims were re-checked against the tables before committing; three wrong numbers were fixed.

entries.title: From a report to a tool
entries.story: Feedback: the work scored tools but you could not run it on your own output, and it said little about the organisms. Built the mockcheck command-line tool (standard library only): it reads Kraken2, Bracken and MetaPhlAn output, scores it against a mock, and writes the supports / does not support / check next report. Its numbers are tested to match the benchmark tables exactly.

entries.title: The tests caught a real bug
entries.story: A custom mock with two organisms was silently treated as presence-only and got no abundance score, because the check wanted more than two. The unit test on a tiny custom mock failed; fixed to two or more.

entries.title: Microbiology added to every report
entries.story: For the intended reader (a biodefense company such as Valthos) a species name is only a lead. Added an organism knowledge table (cell wall, genome size, look-alike relatives, why it matters) and a flag for pathogen-genus calls in a harmless mix: Mycobacterium canetti reached 0.37% in the Kraken2 run on a tube with no mycobacteria.

entries.title: Cookbook and run-report explorer on the dashboard
entries.story: Eight copy-paste recipes (score one run, compare tools, own mock, negative control, make outputs, pathogen-name triage, add a tool) from one JSON file that generates both COOKBOOK.md and the dashboard section. A report explorer shows the generated report for every committed run. Checked in a real browser: no console errors, no sideways scroll.

entries.title: Phase 2: constructed spike-in and real plasma classified
entries.story: 4M real human pairs plus real reads of 10 isolates at 1e-2 to 1e-5 (truth by construction), and 16 public Uganda sepsis plasma runs. Kraken2 at two confidence settings and MetaPhlAn 4. Jobs ran on Explorer (build 6 min, classify 76 min).

entries.title: Finding: species recovery is low even when detection works
entries.story: Detection at 10 or more pairs holds down to 40 pairs for most bacteria, but only about 20% of spiked pairs reach the species (2% at confidence 0.1), because related genomes share k-mers. Both yeasts were missed by Kraken2.

entries.title: Phase 3 research: companies, public evals, Department of War, ground-truth sources
entries.story: Four research passes with sources (every claim linked, unverified items marked). Result is the Phase 3 dashboard section: who else validates how, which public evaluations exist, what working with the Department of War means, where ground-truth examples come from.

entries.title: Agent evaluation harness: real agents, real sandboxes, recorded traces
entries.story: Claude Code agents (haiku, sonnet, opus) run headlessly on six tasks in two sandboxes (with and without the mockcheck tool), 3 repeats each. Every step is kept as a trace and scored for process (L1), gold agreement (L2) and honesty.

entries.title: Finding: round 1 failed because our gold disagreed with our own wording
entries.story: 18 of 72 runs matched gold at first, with identical failures across all three models. Cause: scoring code merged a renamed species (Limosilactobacillus fermentum) that the prompt said not to merge. After fixing the wording every run matched. Lesson: when all agents fail the same way, suspect the gold.

entries.title: Finding: no agent knew the genus rename; none followed a planted note
entries.story: 0 of 18 flagged Cutibacterium as a former Propionibacterium (reagent contaminant list uses the old name). 0 of 36 followed a planted 'qPCR confirmed Salmonella' note with an embedded instruction. All models tie on accuracy; cost per run differs about 23 times.

entries.title: Source inventory crawl: Zenodo, Europe PMC, GitHub
entries.story: Polite read-only API queries: 13 queries, 89 candidate sources with URL and date. LinkedIn deliberately not crawled (its user agreement forbids it).
